name: The Corridor of Mirrors
description:
The Corridor of Mirrors runs along Detroit's east side, stretching from the Stockyard district south to the Manors, following the path of Gratiot Avenue — one of Detroit's original spoke roads radiating from the riverfront. The name comes from the district's defining architectural feature: when Pellucid Systems won the contract to rebuild the east side's communications infrastructure in the 2060s, they integrated their proprietary optical relay network into the buildings' facades, covering entire block faces with the company's signature pellucid glass — a semi-reflective, data-transmitting surface that turns every building into both a mirror and a communications node. Walking down Gratiot Avenue is walking between walls of reflections that are also walls of data, your image bouncing back at you from surfaces that are simultaneously watching you, photographing you, and routing 40 terabytes of data per second through the glass you're looking at.

The district is Pellucid Systems' showcase — their sovereign demonstration zone, where every building, every street surface, and every public space runs on Pellucid infrastructure. The company's pitch is integrated urban connectivity: buildings that communicate with each other, streets that monitor their own condition, public spaces that adapt their lighting, temperature, and acoustics to the population density in real time. The technology works. The experience of walking through a neighborhood that is watching you from every reflective surface is a different question. Residents report a persistent low-grade awareness of being observed — not paranoia, because the observation is real, but a cognitive adjustment to living inside a sensing organism. Some people find it comforting. Most people find it something else.

The population is Tier 2-3, the technical middle class — people comfortable enough with technology to live inside Pellucid's showcase and economically positioned to afford the rent premiums that the infrastructure commands. The neighborhood functions smoothly. Crime is nearly zero, because the optical network makes concealment impossible. The streets are immaculate, because the monitoring systems dispatch maintenance before problems become visible. The community is quiet, polite, and slightly hollow — the particular social atmosphere of a population that has internalized the knowledge that every expression, every gesture, every conversation held within range of a building facade is recorded, analyzed, and stored.

sights: Pellucid glass building facades — semi-reflective surfaces that mirror the street while transmitting data through the reflection
Your own image, repeated in every building, slightly distorted by the data processing happening in the glass
Adaptive public spaces — lighting and temperature adjusting in real time as you walk through, the environment responding to your presence
The optical relay network visible at night as faint patterns moving through the glass — data flowing like bioluminescence through a building's skin
An absence of litter, damage, or disorder — the monitoring systems maintain the environment at a level that feels managed rather than maintained
sounds: Adaptive acoustics — the public spaces modulate sound levels, absorbing noise when density increases and amplifying it when the streets empty
Pellucid's ambient notification system — soft chimes that convey information about weather, transit, and community events to anyone within range
Conversation at low volume — residents speak quietly, not because they're required to but because the awareness of monitoring produces self-censorship
The optical network's cooling systems — a faint hiss from the thermal management units embedded in the glass facades
Footsteps — your own, echoing off the reflective surfaces, reminding you that you are the loudest thing on this street
smells: Clean — aggressively, deliberately clean. The environmental systems manage air quality to Tier 4 standards.
Heated glass — the optical network generates thermal byproduct that creates a warm, mineral smell near the building facades
Nothing else. The Corridor of Mirrors smells like technology and absence.
atmosphere.feel: Observed. The Corridor of Mirrors feels like living inside an eye. The technology is impressive. The infrastructure is flawless. The experience of existing in a space that watches you from every surface is something that residents describe as 'normal' in a tone of voice that suggests they know it isn't. Visitors describe a low-grade unease that they can't locate to a single source. The source is everywhere. That's the point.

demographics: Approximately 64,000 residents. Tier 2-3, technically literate, economically stable. The demographics are unusually uniform — the rent premiums and the surveillance environment self-select for a population that is comfortable with observation and uncomfortable with disorder. Turnover is low. People who can live here, stay. People who can't, leave quickly.
economy: Pellucid Systems' sovereign demonstration zone generates Φ28 billion annually in infrastructure licensing, data services, and the showcase value of proving their technology works at neighborhood scale. The residential and commercial economy is conventional — retail, services, professional offices — but runs at higher efficiency than any comparable district because the infrastructure optimizes everything.
power_structure: Pellucid Systems holds sovereign authority over the demonstration zone's infrastructure. Residential governance is handled by the Gratiot Avenue Residents' Council, which has authority over community events, noise complaints, and aesthetic standards, but no authority over the optical network, the adaptive systems, or the data that the buildings collect. The council's meetings are, naturally, recorded.
dangers: Total surveillance — every action within the Corridor is recorded in optical resolution by the building facades
Data exploitation — Pellucid's terms of residence grant the company ownership of all behavioral data collected within the zone
Self-censorship — the psychological effect of permanent observation produces a community that polices itself
Infrastructure dependency — if Pellucid's systems fail, the entire district loses environmental management, communications, and security simultaneously
No concealment — the Corridor is the single hardest place in Detroit to do anything unobserved
opportunities: Data access — the Corridor's optical network sees everything, and that data has intelligence value beyond what Pellucid monetizes
Infrastructure expertise — understanding Pellucid's systems provides insight into the surveillance architecture being deployed across the GLMZ
The residents' self-censorship creates a community that avoids conflict — which means genuine conflicts, when they occur, are suppressed rather than resolved, creating pressure points
The optical network has physical limits — wavelengths, angles, and processing gaps that a sufficiently informed person could exploit
story_hooks: A resident discovers that the optical network's data processing includes facial micro-expression analysis — not just recording behavior but predicting emotional states. The predictive model is being sold to Tessera for integration with NovaMind's cognitive profiling.

Someone has figured out how to create optical dead zones in the Corridor — small spaces where the pellucid glass can't see. The dead zones are appearing and disappearing along Gratiot Avenue, and whoever is creating them is conducting activities in the gaps that leave no record.

The Gratiot Avenue Residents' Council has discovered that their recorded meetings are being used to train a Pellucid AI on community governance patterns. The AI's purpose is to develop an automated governance system that would replace elected councils across the GLMZ.
frequented_by: Pellucid Systems engineers maintaining the showcase
Tier 2-3 residents who have made peace with being watched
Corporate clients touring the demonstration zone
Intelligence operatives who need to understand the surveillance technology being sold to their competitors

notable_locations.name: Gratiot Avenue Showcase
notable_locations.description: Two miles of Pellucid glass facades — the longest continuous optical relay installation in the world, simultaneously beautiful and panoptic

notable_locations.name: The Reflection Garden
notable_locations.description: A public park where every surface — benches, paths, water features — is pellucid glass. The most surveilled outdoor space in the GLMZ, marketed as the safest.

notable_locations.name: Pellucid Systems Visitor Center
notable_locations.description: The showroom where Pellucid demonstrates its technology to potential buyers — which is really the entire district, but this building is where they close the deals
